current.jp: はしのもち方をならいました
current.kana: はしのもちかたをならいました

structure_explanation.en: The target pattern is 〜方（かた）, which attaches to the stem of a verb (the 連用形) to form a noun meaning 'way of doing something'. Here 持つ (to hold) becomes 持ち and, with 方, forms 持ち方 = 'way of holding'. はしの indicates what this way is of (of the chopsticks), を marks this noun as the object, and ならいました (polite past form of 習う) closes the sentence with 'I learned'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O padrão-alvo é 〜方（かた）, que se liga ao radical de um verbo (a forma 連用形) para formar um substantivo que significa 'maneira de fazer algo'. Aqui 持つ (segurar) vira 持ち e, com 方, forma 持ち方 = 'maneira de segurar'. はしの indica de que coisa é essa maneira (dos hashi), を marca esse substantivo como objeto, e ならいました (forma polida passada de 習う) fecha a frase com 'aprendi'.

translation_literal.en: I learned how to hold chopsticks.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto aos hashi, a maneira de segurar, aprendi.

translation.en: I learned how to hold chopsticks.

note.en: stem (連用形) of 持つ, used before the suffix 方
note.pt-BR: radical (連用形) de 持つ, usado antes do sufixo 方

note.en: suffix 〜方 connected to 持ち, forming 'way of holding'
note.pt-BR: sufixo 〜方 ligado a 持ち, formando 'maneira de segurar'

note.en: stem (連用形) of 習う, before the polite auxiliary ます
note.pt-BR: radical (連用形) de 習う, antes do auxiliar polido ます

note.en: ます in the past: まし + た
note.pt-BR: ます no passado: まし + た

objections.objection: translation_literal.pt-BR 'Quanto aos hashi, a maneira de segurar, aprendi.' uses the topic-は mirror for はしの, which is the genitive particle の, not は — the sentence has no topic marker. It is actively harmful here because はし is written in kana and starts with は, so the literal mirror trains the learner to misparse はし as noun+topic-は.
objections.auditor_hint: Dos hashi, a maneira de segurar, aprendi.

current.kana: きょうわあさからはれだ

structure_explanation.en: The topic 今日 (きょう, today) is marked by は and sets the scene of the sentence. 朝から (あさから) means 'since morning', with から indicating the starting point in time. The core is 晴れ (はれ), a noun describing fine weather/clear skies, closed by the copula だ. The focus here is the vocabulary 晴れ (sunny weather).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O tópico 今日 (きょう, hoje) é marcado por は e dá o cenário da frase. 朝から (あさから) significa 'desde de manhã', com から indicando o ponto de partida no tempo. O núcleo é 晴れ (はれ), um substantivo que descreve o tempo bom/céu limpo, fechado pela cópula だ. O foco aqui é o vocabulário 晴れ (tempo ensolarado).

translation_literal.en: As for today, it's been nice weather since morning.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a hoje, desde a manhã (é) tempo bom.

translation.en: Today it's been nice out since morning.

objections.objection: Ungrammatical pt-BR left in learner-facing text: "朝から (あさから) significa 'desde de manhã'". 'desde de' is not valid Portuguese. The same record had its pt accent typo ('esta'→'está') fixed by this patch, so shipping this one alongside it is inconsistent.

current.jp: 先生は丁寧な日本語を話します
current.kana: せんせいわていねいなにほんごをはなします

structure_explanation.en: The topic 先生 (teacher) is marked by は. Here 丁寧 appears as a na-adjective modifying a noun, so it comes with な (丁寧な日本語 = 'careful/polite Japanese'). 日本語 is the object marked by を, and the main verb is 話す (to speak) in the polite present with ます. Contrast: before a noun, 丁寧 takes な; in adverbial position it takes に (丁寧に).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O tópico 先生 (professor) é marcado por は. Aqui 丁寧 aparece como adjetivo-na modificando um substantivo, por isso vem com な (丁寧な日本語 = 'um japonês cuidadoso/educado'). 日本語 é o objeto marcado por を, e o verbo principal é 話す (falar) no presente polido com ます. Note o contraste com a frase anterior: antes de substantivo usa-se な; em posição de advérbio usa-se に.

translation_literal.en: As for the teacher, he speaks polite Japanese.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao professor, (ele) educado/cuidadoso japonês fala.

translation.pt-BR: O professor fala um japonês cuidadoso.

note.en: な-adjective 丁寧 modifying a noun, requires な
note.pt-BR: adjetivo-na 丁寧 modificando substantivo, exige な

note.en: connective stem (連用形) of 話す, base for ます
note.pt-BR: raiz conectiva (連用形) de 話す, base para ます

note.en: ます in the polite present, attached to 話し
note.pt-BR: ます no presente polido, anexado a 話し

objections.objection: The op is only half-applied. Its own text says the dangling cross-reference is 'also in expl_pt ("a frase anterior")', but only structure_explanation.en was rewritten. pt-BR still ends with 'Note o contraste com a frase anterior: antes de substantivo usa-se な; em posição de advérbio usa-se に'. The defect the op was filed against still ships in the learner's own language, and en/pt-BR now diverge in content (locale-parity break).
objections.auditor_hint: …com ます. Contraste: antes de substantivo, 丁寧 recebe な; em posição adverbial, recebe に (丁寧に).

current.jp: 適当な言葉が見つからない
current.kana: てきとうなことばがみつからない

structure_explanation.en: 適当 is a na-adjective (adjectival noun) and therefore links to the noun 言葉 (word) by means of な, forming 適当な言葉 (suitable/right word). が marks this phrase as the subject, and the verb 見つかる (to be found, intransitive) appears in the negative form 見つからない. Note that 見つかる is intransitive, so the English 'I can't find' sounds more natural than the literal 'it isn't found'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: 適当 é um な-adjetivo (substantivo adjetival) e por isso liga-se ao substantivo 言葉 (palavra) por meio de な, formando 適当な言葉 (palavra adequada/certa). が marca esse sintagma como sujeito, e o verbo 見つかる (ser encontrado, intransitivo) aparece na forma negativa 見つからない. Note que 見つかる é intransitivo, então o português 'não consigo achar' soa mais natural que o literal 'não se encontra'.

translation_literal.en: The right word does not come to me.
translation_literal.pt-BR: A palavra adequada não se encontra.

translation.en: I can't find the right word.
translation.pt-BR: Não consigo achar a palavra certa.

note.en: adnominal na-adjective: 適当 + な before the noun
note.pt-BR: な-adjetivo adnominal: 適当 + な antes do substantivo

note.en: な (adnominal form of だ) linking 適当 to 言葉
note.pt-BR: な (forma adnominal de だ) que liga 適当 a 言葉

gloss.en: to be found, to turn up

note.en: negative stem of 見つかる (見つから + ない)
note.pt-BR: raiz negativa de 見つかる (見つから + ない)

note.en: auxiliary ない negating 見つかる
note.pt-BR: auxiliar ない que nega 見つかる

objections.objection: Collateral damage from the fix. Before, expl_en said "the Portuguese 'I can't find' sounds more natural than the literal 'it isn't found'" — true, because translation_literal.pt-BR is 'A palavra adequada não se encontra'. After swapping Portuguese→English, the sentence now asserts the literal English is 'it isn't found', but translation_literal.en reads 'The right word does not come to me'. The fix moved a true claim onto a language where the record contradicts itself.
objections.auditor_hint: Either set translation_literal.en to 'The right word is not found.', or reword expl_en to: "…so English prefers 'I can't find' over a word-for-word 'the right word is not found'."

current.jp: この中でどれが好きですか
current.kana: このなかでどれがすきですか

structure_explanation.en: この中で ("within this set") delimits the group from which one chooses, with で indicating the scope of the comparison. どれ marked by が is the item one likes. 好き is a な-adjective (形状詞) functioning as "to like", and what is liked comes with が. どれ asks "which?" among three or more.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: この中で ("dentro deste conjunto") delimita o grupo de onde se escolhe, com で indicando o âmbito da comparação. どれ marcado por が é o item de que se gosta. 好き é um adjetivo-な (形状詞) que funciona como "gostar de", e o que se gosta vem com が. どれ pergunta "qual?" entre três ou mais.

translation_literal.en: Among these, which one do you like?
translation_literal.pt-BR: Dentro disto, quanto a qual, é gostável?

translation.en: Which of these do you like?

note.en: na-adjective 好き used as a predicate with です
note.pt-BR: adjetivo-な 好き usado como predicado com です

note.en: polite form of the copula (です)

objections.objection: translation_literal.pt-BR 'Dentro disto, quanto a qual, é gostável?' applies the 'Quanto a X' topic-は mirror to どれが — the sentence contains no は at all, が is the subject/target marker of 好き. This is the identical defect the batch just corrected in sent:gen-49a9d44f8f0c (みんなが), so leaving it is internally inconsistent with the patch's own standard. ('gostável' is also not a pt-BR word.)
